Lecture 4: Stacks and Queues
What is a stack?
A stack is a linear data structure.
Items are added and removed at one end, called the top.
It follows Last In, First Out (LIFO).
Stack operations
push(x) adds x to the top.
pop() removes and returns the top item.
peek() returns the top item without removing it.
Popping an empty stack is an error called underflow.
Applications of stacks
Function calls are tracked on a call stack.
Undo in a text editor uses a stack of changes.
Balanced brackets are checked with a stack.
What is a queue?
A queue is a linear data structure.
Items join at the rear and leave from the front.
It follows First In, First Out (FIFO).
Queue operations
enqueue(x) adds x at the rear.
dequeue() removes and returns the front item.
A circular array reuses freed slots: rear = (rear + 1) mod n.
